Keyboard DJing · macOS · pre-alpha

manadj

DJ from your keyboard. Keep what works.

Play with your keyboard and mouse on four Decks. When a blend works, listen back to the Take, adjust the timing or fades, and keep it for another Set. Your library and the blends you've saved stay together in manadj.

Take the tour ↓ Source on GitHub

  1. PLAYMix with your keyboard and mouse
  2. CAPTUREListen back to your Takes

01 · PERFORM

Two hands. Up to four Decks.

in the app: PERFORM view

Use your keyboard and mouse to mix on four Decks. Keys choose the control; mouse movement rides it. Your Library stays below the waveforms, ready for the next Track.

  • Press D or K to play the focused left or right Deck.
  • Hold Q or P and move the mouse to sweep its filter.
  • Hold G or H and move the mouse to ride channel volume; double-tap to cut or return to full volume.

KBD labels show keys on the controls. F1 opens help. Key Lock is on by default.

Prefer to grab a Track? Drag it from the Library onto a Deck to load it. For a different blend, split a Track into stems and mute or solo its vocals, drums, bass, or other instruments while you play.

02 · CAPTURE

Hear that blend again

in the app: Sessions · HISTORY

While you mix live, manadj logs Deck and Mixer events in a Session, not an audio recording. Detected handovers become Takes; a tease that returns to the original Track can become a Cameo Take.

Find a moment on the timeline and replay it through the Decks. Grab a fader to take over live, or cut out a missed blend by hand for review. Compare a few attempts, then Promote the ones you want to use again.

  • Session
  • Take
  • Cameo
03 · EDIT

Rework the good ones

in the app: EDIT view

Open a Take in the Mix editor as an editable draft. Captured fades become envelopes you can reshape; jumps stay editable too. Change where a Track enters, shorten a fade, or adjust a cut, then audition through the same Decks and Mixer you use live.

Promote saves the draft as a Transition you can use again. The original Take stays intact. The same timeline handles Cameos and multi-Track Routines, and you can start from a blank mix when you already know what you want to try.

  • Mix editor
  • Transition
  • Cameo
  • Routine
  • Promote
04 · SETS

Plan the blends. Play the Set.

in the app: library sidebar · Sets

Arrange Tracks in a Set and choose how each hands over: a saved Transition, a Take you've selected, or a hard cut. Leave a handover Unresolved to use the pair's best saved Transition, falling back to a cut if there isn't one.

Press Play set and the Conductor executes those handovers on the Decks and Mixer. Touch a Deck or Mixer control to take over; the music keeps playing. Pick up resumes the plan when your live Deck state lines up with it.

  • Set
  • Unresolved
  • Conductor
  • Pickup
05 · FOLLOW

Your past mixes help pick the next Track

in the app: any track list

Turn on Follow for a Deck to see next-Track suggestions as you play. The list follows what's loaded, so you can keep browsing while the mix changes.

Your choices come first: Known pairs connected by a saved Transition, Cameo, or a Linked association. Repeated live pairs come next as Observed. Then Compatible suggestions draw on Key, Tags, shared artists, BPM, and Energy. A clashing Key alone doesn't rule a Track out. For more variety, Temperature reshuffles the Compatible suggestions without moving them above your curated pairs.

  • Follow mode
  • Known
  • Observed
  • Compatible
  • Linked
06 · CURATE

Keep your Library in order

in the app: EXPORT view

Drop audio files or folders from Finder onto the Library to import them in place, or onto a Playlist to add them there too.

Work through Unprocessed Tracks, clean up names, and add your own Tags, grouped into Tag Categories such as Genre or Vibe. Set Energy from 1–5 to reflect how a Track feels to you.

Playlists preserve your chosen play order even when you sort the table. Mark a Track Archived to remove it from the active Library without deleting its file or metadata.

07 · ANALYSIS

Prepare the next Track

in the app: automatic · Settings › Waveforms

New Tracks are analyzed for Beatgrid, Key, waveform, and Structure. If beat detection fails, the Track is flagged for attention. Energy estimates appear where you haven't set a rating.

When you're ready, stamp Hot Cues 1–4 as a ladder into the detected drop. Only empty slots are filled; analysis doesn't write cues on its own. Adjust the drop cue yourself when your ears disagree.

CUE LADDER 1first buildup 2−16 bars 3−8 bars 4drop

08 · SYNC

Take your Library to Engine DJ or Rekordbox

in the app: SYNC view

The Sync inbox shows missing Tracks and metadata differences across your music folder, manadj, Engine DJ, and Rekordbox. Export sends Library metadata and playlists out; Tags become playlists in Engine DJ. External Import brings back changes such as cues set at a gig.

Export is off by default. Enable it in Settings when you're ready to write to an external library.

  • Export
  • External Import
09 · ACQUIRE

Bring your SoundCloud finds into the Library

in the app: SYNC › Acquisition

Refresh your SoundCloud likes to see what you already own and choose what to download. Mixes and clips are filtered out by default, and downloaded titles and artist names are cleaned up.

If SoundCloud can't supply the audio, search Soulseek and choose a file. manadj records where its downloads came from, ready for you to curate alongside the rest of your Library.

  • Source Item
10 · CONTROL

Plug in a Controller

in the app: plug in · Settings › Jog calibration

Prefer physical controls? A supported Controller drives the same Decks and Mixer, with pad and transport lights following the app.

Mappings are available for Pioneer DDJ-GRV6, Pioneer DDJ-SB3, and Hercules DJControl Inpulse 300 MK2. The GRV6 controls all four Decks and Beat FX; the SB3 uses a layer switch to reach Decks C and D.

WORDS

The words manadj uses

the same names appear in the app
Archived
Out of your active library. Nothing is deleted, and it never comes back on its own. Reversible.
Beatgrid
Where every beat falls in a Track. BPM is read from it.
Cameo
A guest Track that drops in over a host Track and leaves again — a double or a tease.
Compatible
Tracks whose tempo fits and whose Key, Tags, or shared artist suggest a match. Energy helps rank them.
Conductor
Plays a Set on the Decks and Mixer. A manual Deck or Mixer gesture hands control back to you.
Controller
A MIDI DJ controller driving the Decks, Mixer, and library browsing.
Cue mode
What a Hot Cue does on a paused Deck. Gated previews while held; Trigger starts playback.
Cue-slot convention
Hot Cues 1–4 lead into the drop. 4 is the drop; 3 is 8 bars before, 2 is 16 bars before, and 1 is typically 32 bars before.
Deck
One of four players, A–D. A Deck keeps playing when you switch views.
Energy
How intense a Track is, 1–5. Its own field, not a Tag.
Export
Pushes your Library out to Engine DJ, Rekordbox, or file tags. manadj's values win.
External Import
Pulls things you changed downstream back in, like cues set at a gig or Keys analyzed in Engine.
Follow mode
Keeps the track list filtered to good next Tracks for what is playing.
Hot Cue
One of 8 saved positions in a Track that you jump to while playing.
Key Lock
Keeps a Track in its Key while you move the pitch fader.
Known
Tracks connected by something you did — Linked, or a saved Transition or Cameo.
Linked
Your one-tap note that two Tracks go well together.
Mix editor
One timeline for editing any Transition, Cameo, or Routine, or reviewing a Take.
Mixer
Trim, 3-band EQ, filter, and fader per Deck, plus crossfader, master, and Beat FX.
Observed
A pair you have mixed more than once without saving anything for it.
Pickup
Hand control back to the Conductor from where the Decks are now.
Playlist
A hand-ordered list of Tracks, curated in manadj and Exported.
Promote
Turning a reviewed Take into a saved Transition (or Cameo, or Routine).
Quantize
Snaps cue placement and loops to beats; Hot Cue jumps preserve the playing Deck's beat phase.
Routine
A saved passage weaving three or more Track slots, captured live or authored in the Mix editor.
Session
The record of one stretch of playing, timed to the moment. Controls only, no audio.
Set
Tracks in order, where each handover points at a Transition, a Take, or a hard cut.
Setup guide
Planned for the first release — a short, skippable flow that sets up one thing, rerunnable from Settings.
Source Item
A track on SoundCloud you've liked and might want to download.
Structure
A Track split into intro, buildup, drop, breakdown, and outro, found by Analysis.
SYNC
Decks join one shared tempo. Move any member's pitch and the group follows.
Tag
A label you put on a Track. Every Tag belongs to one Tag Category.
Tag Category
A named, colored, ordered group of Tags — Genre, Vibe, Role.
Take
A blend between two Tracks, captured automatically while you play.
Tour
Pointers to the main controls, shown the first time you open each area.
Track
An audio file plus everything you know about it — title, artist, Key, BPM, Energy, Tags, Hot Cues.
Transition
A saved move from one Track into another, with alignment, fades, EQ, and filter moves.
Unprocessed track
Added but not yet curated — no Tags, title and artist not cleaned up.
Unresolved
A handover in a Set with nothing pinned. It uses your best saved Transition for the pair.
